summary: TechCrunch's Week in Review newsletter for the week of Nov. 11, 2023 recaps OpenAI's first developer conference, Apple hardware reviews, and Tim Cook's comments on generative AI. It also covers Ford shutting down VIIZR, WeWork's Chapter 11 filing, Bumble naming Slack CEO Lidiane Jones as its new CEO, and Arrival's struggles. The issue closes with podcast and TechCrunch+ highlights on Klarna, superconductors and the 'unicorn' term.
one_line: TechCrunch's weekly roundup covering OpenAI's dev day, M3 Mac reviews, WeWork's bankruptcy, Bumble's new CEO Lidiane Jones, and more tech news.
key_facts: OpenAI hosted its first-ever developer conference on Monday, announcing tools to create custom "GPTs", new text-to-speech models, a DALL-E 3 API, and GPT-4 Turbo.
Brian found the M3 iMac 24-inch lacking and not necessarily worth the upgrade from the 2021 model, apart from the M3 chip's "impressive" gains over the M1.
The 16-inch M3 Max MacBook Pro costs $2,500 (plus pricey add-ons) and splits the difference between the Mac Studio and MacBook Air, per Brian's review.
Mozilla senior director of content Carolyn O'Hara outlined Mozilla's fediverse strategy, built on decentralized apps like Mastodon that communicate over the ActivityPub protocol.

Ford shut down VIIZR, a majority Ford-owned SaaS company with Salesforce as a minority investor, announced in December 2021, which built an app for tradespeople to schedule appointments and send invoices.
Tim Cook pushed back on the idea that Apple is behind in AI on the Q4 earnings call; reports suggest Apple is on track to spend $1 billion per year on generative AI.
WeWork filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, listing over $18.6 billion of debt; it was co-founded by Adam Neumann and backed by SoftBank, BlackRock and Goldman Sachs.
Bumble is replacing founder CEO Whitney Wolfe Herd with Slack CEO Lidiane Jones, who became Slack CEO last year succeeding Stewart Butterfield.
EV startup Arrival, founded eight years ago to make EV production "radically more efficient", faces missed production targets, low cash reserves, layoffs and a pivot.

Equity covered fintech market signs starting with Klarna's Q3 results; Found featured Nasrat Khalid of Aseel, which began as an Afghan artisan e-commerce company and now delivers humanitarian aid in Afghanistan and Turkey.
A new supposedly room-temperature superconducting material is facing retraction of its Nature-published paper, per Tim's TechCrunch+ piece.
Klarna started a legal entity restructuring to set up a U.K. holding company as an early step toward an IPO.
Aileen Lee of Cowboy Ventures coined the term "unicorns" 10 years ago, and her venture firm is also a decade old.
